# TrueFoundry Provider

The TrueFoundry provider manages [TrueFoundry](https://www.truefoundry.com)
AI Gateway resources on a TrueFoundry control plane:

- **Model access** — [provider accounts](resources/provider_account.md) (OpenAI,
  Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Foundry, AWS Bedrock, virtual models) and the models
  exposed through them, plus [custom endpoint accounts](resources/custom_endpoint_account.md)
  for arbitrary HTTP services proxied by the gateway. The
  [models data source](data-sources/models.md) lists everything on the gateway.
- **Gateway configuration** — budget rules
  ([tenant](resources/tenant_budget_config.md) and
  [team](resources/team_budget_config.md) scoped; the
  [deprecated v1 config](resources/gateway_budget_config.md) has a
  [migration guide](guides/budget-limiting-v2.md)), plus the tenant-wide
  singletons for [data access](resources/gateway_data_access_config.md),
  [data routing](resources/gateway_data_routing_config.md), and
  [guardrail wiring](resources/gateway_guardrails_config.md), and
  [guardrail groups](resources/guardrail_group.md) (Azure Prompt Shield and
  Content Safety).
- **Platform integrations** — [Azure blob storage](resources/azure_account.md),
  [Slack notification channels](resources/slack_account.md),
  [HashiCorp Vault secret stores](resources/hashicorp_account.md), the
  [built-in system secret store](resources/system_secret_store.md), and the
  [secret groups](resources/secret_group.md) whose secrets every credential
  attribute can reference.
- **Access** — [virtual accounts](resources/virtual_account.md) (service
  accounts) with scoped permissions and token handling, and custom
  [roles](resources/role.md) that `role_id` references resolve against.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    truefoundry = {
      source = "terraform.staffbase.com/staffbase/truefoundry"
    }
  }
}

# Credentials can also come from the TFY_HOST / TFY_API_KEY environment variables.
provider "truefoundry" {
  host    = "https://my-org.truefoundry.cloud"
  api_key = var.truefoundry_api_key
}
```

## Authentication

The provider authenticates against the control plane with a Bearer API token.
`host` and `api_key` can be set in the provider block or via the `TFY_HOST`
and `TFY_API_KEY` environment variables.

The API key can be a personal access token or a virtual account token. For
CI/CD, prefer a dedicated [virtual account](resources/virtual_account.md) whose
permissions are limited to the resources Terraform manages.

## Handling secrets

Every credential attribute (API keys, connection strings, webhook URLs, bot
tokens, …) accepts either a raw value or a TrueFoundry secret reference such as
`my-tenant:hashicorp:vault-secrets:secret-store:vault::path/value`.

**Prefer secret references.** The control plane returns credential values as
stored: secret references round-trip cleanly and enable drift detection, while
raw values end up in the Terraform state (and, on refresh or import, are read
back into it). Secret references can point at a
[HashiCorp Vault secret store](resources/hashicorp_account.md) or the
[system secret store](resources/system_secret_store.md) — both manageable with
this provider.

## Importing existing resources

All resources support `terraform import`: accounts and guardrail groups by
their FQN, virtual accounts by their control plane ID, and the gateway config
singletons by fixed string IDs. Each resource page documents the exact syntax.

Only import resources whose features this provider models — an apply would
strip unsupported features (e.g. Azure certificate auth, advanced routing
options, non-blob-storage Azure integrations) from a pre-existing manifest.
See the resource descriptions and the
[repository README](https://github.com/Staffbase/terraform-provider-truefoundry#known-limitations)
for the full list of limitations.

## Schema

### Optional

- `api_key` (String, Sensitive) TrueFoundry API key (personal access token or virtual account token). Can also be set via the TFY_API_KEY environment variable.
- `host` (String) Base URL of the TrueFoundry control plane, e.g. https://my-org.truefoundry.cloud. Can also be set via the TFY_HOST environment variable.
